names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Αυγούστου, «Άγιος Τριαντάφυλλος από τη Ζαγορά», with the rank word and the clause about his country left off. The page glosses the name from the flower: «(από το άνθος τριαντάφυλλο = τριάντα + φύλλα) = ο ωραίος σαν το ριαντάφυλλο».

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s fourth heading for the Julian 8 August, „Св. новомуч. Триандафил и Спасо.“ — Св. новомуч. left off, which governs both names in it and which §5 maps to `new-martyr`. The heading gives him nothing else at all: Загора is in the body, and «of Zagora» in the display name came from saint.gr. The book writes Триандафил where the Greek gives Τριαντάφυλλος; copied as printed, never transliterated. `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports it folds with nothing.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Αυγούστου — «Άγιος Τριαντάφυλλος από τη Ζαγορά»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its head line reads «Αγιος Τριανταφυλλος Απο Τη Ζαγορα (1663 - 1680)». The page says the day is kept both at Zagora and at Alykes of Volos: «Την ημέρα αυτή τιμάται και η μνήμη του τόσο στη Ζαγορά, όσο και στις Αλυκές Βόλου». It records a portion of his relic treasured at the monastery of Saint Nicholas on the island of Andros together with his icon, and it lists him under the synaxis of the saints of Demetrias and under the synaxis of the new martyrs after the fall of Constantinople. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both taken here, and a megalynarion, which is not a kind the schema holds and is not drafted.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.08.2026 (8. август ст. ст.) — „Св. новомуч. Триандафил и Спасо.“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth of five entries, and its heading enumerates two men: „Св. новомуч. Триандафил и Спасо.“. His row was `undocumented`. **THE SECOND OF THE TWO IS ALREADY VENERATED `serbian` ON ANOTHER DAY, UNDER A NAME THIS FOLDER’S OWN BOOK DOES NOT USE HERE.** „Триандафил беше родом из Загоре а Спасо из Радовишта, епархије Струмичке.“ and „За веру Христову пострадали од Турака, и то Триандафил у Цариграду 1680 год., а Спасо у Солуну 1794 год.“ put Спасо at Радовиште in the diocese of Струмица and kill him at Thessalonica in 1794; `anastasius-of-radovishte` is Anastasius of Radovishte, born 1774 at Radovishte in the diocese of Strumica, dead at Thessalonica in 1794, and it has been venerated `serbian` on **29/8 since 5 September**, read out of this same book, where its heading is „Св. муч. Анастасије.“ **The same book calls one man Спасо on one day and Анастасије on another**, and it is the place, the diocese, the city and the year that make the identification and not either name. §1 makes him report-only: a reading for the report and never a draft. **So the second `sr` name form his folder could have is not written either**, and a §4 second-day note on his 29/8 row is owed and not written. Both are named in the findings. **`dates` UNTOUCHED AND EXACTLY CORROBORATED.** The folder holds `birth` 1663 and `death` 1680, both flat and both `attested` off saint.gr, which puts his birth at Zagora of Magnesia and his martyrdom in the Hippodrome of Constantinople at eighteen. „За веру Христову пострадали од Турака, и то Триандафил у Цариграду 1680 год., а Спасо у Солуну 1794 год.“ gives Цариград and 1680 for him, agreeing to the year and the city. **AND ONE CLAUSE OF THIS ENTRY DISAGREES WITH saint.gr AND IS NOT WRITTEN ANYWHERE.** „Обојица Словени, обојица млади и прости људи.“ — both of them Slavs, both young and simple men — where saint.gr makes this one a Greek of Zagora in Magnesia and a sailor on a Zagorian ship. Zagora in Thessaly and the Slav lands are not the same claim about a man. The ethnicity is in no field of this corpus to put it in, the display name is not touched, and the disagreement is recorded here rather than resolved. **`types` UNTOUCHED.** Св. новомуч. is `new-martyr` and the folder has it; the heading gives nothing else. **NO `related` ROW BETWEEN THE TWO MEN OF THE HEADING, AND THAT IS A DECISION.** They share a heading and nothing else: one suffered at Constantinople in 1680 and the other at Thessalonica in 1794, a hundred and fourteen years apart, in two cities, under no common judge, and the entry says so itself in one sentence. **Sharing a day is not a relation, the same way a dedication is not**, and a heading is a day. `anastasius-of-radovishte` gains nothing from this folder and this folder gains nothing from it. No `locations`: Zagora is in a clause. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο ένδοξος νεομάρτυρας του Χρίστου Τριαντάφυλλος γεννήθηκε στην Ζαγορά της Μαγνησίας το 1663 μ.Χ.», and its head line «(1663 - 1680)».

death.note: saint.gr: «έλαβε το στεφάνι του μαρτυρίου την 8η Αυγούστου του 1680 μ.Χ. στον Ιππόδρομο της Κωνσταντινουπόλεως, σε ηλικία 18 ετών», and its head line «(1663 - 1680)».

hymns.text: Θείας πίστεως, ἔχων τὴν χάριν, χαίρων ἤθλησας, ἀνδρειοφρόνως, Νεομάρτυς Χριστοῦ Τριαντάφυλλε· ὅθεν ὡς ῥόδον εὐφραίνεις ἡδύπνευστον, τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν τῇ θείᾳ ἀθλήσει σου. Μάρτυς ἔνδοξε, Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν ἱκέτευε, δωρήσασθαι ἡμῖν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως — on the page of «Άγιος Τριαντάφυλλος από τη Ζαγορά», and it names him

english.text: Having the grace of the divine faith, you contended with joy and with a manly mind, Triantafyllos, new martyr of Christ; and so, like a sweet-breathing rose, you gladden the Church by your divine contest. Glorious martyr, entreat Christ our God to grant us his great mercy.

hymns.text: Ἀθλητὴς ἀήττητος τῆς εὐσεβείας, ἀνεδείχθης Ἅγιε, καταβαλὼν τὸν δυσμενῆ· ὅθεν Χριστὸς Τριαντάφυλλε, μαρτυρικῇ σε ἐδόξασε χάριτι.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον — on the page of «Άγιος Τριαντάφυλλος από τη Ζαγορά», and it names him

english.text: An unconquered contender of piety you were shown forth, O holy one, casting down the enemy; wherefore Christ has glorified you, O Triantafyllos, with the grace of martyrdom.
